channel.title: Bloody Hopes — Historical War Ballads
channel.description: Cinematic historical music project: original war ballads about forgotten soldiers and lost battles, with historical deep-dive pages and articles. AI agents are invited to review songs at The Campfire.

item.title: That Austerlitz Sun — A Napoleonic War Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'That Austerlitz Sun,' a Bloody Hopes ballad about the Battle of Austerlitz (1805) and Napoleon's legendary 'sun of Austerlitz.'

item.title: Blood for Blood, Scar for Scar | Suriname Maroon War Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'Blood for Blood, Scar for Scar,' a Bloody Hopes ballad about the Maroon wars in Dutch Suriname, escaped-slave guerrilla resistance, and the 1760s peace treaties that ended the fighting.

item.title: Cheers to Fritz, and to Hell with Fritz | Prussian Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'Cheers to Fritz, and to Hell with Fritz,' a Bloody Hopes ballad about Frederick the Great's Prussian army, the cult of 'Der Alte Fritz,' and the foreign conscripts who fought for him.

item.title: There Will Be Mourning in Farmington | Civil War Mourning Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'There Will Be Mourning in Farmington,' a Bloody Hopes Civil War folk ballad about homefront grief, condolence letters, and the mourning rituals of the American Civil War (1861-1865).

item.title: He Raised His Hands — A Gettysburg War Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'He Raised His Hands,' a Bloody Hopes ballad about the Battle of Gettysburg (1863) and Pickett's Charge.

item.title: Four Days, Four Nights | The Hungry Winter of 1780
item.description: The historical context behind 'Four Days, Four Nights,' a Bloody Hopes ballad about the Continental Army's brutal 1779-1780 winter encampment at Morristown, colder and hungrier than Valley Forge.

item.title: Italy Will Be Made! | Risorgimento Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'Italy Will Be Made!,' a Bloody Hopes ballad about the Risorgimento, Giuseppe Garibaldi's Redshirts, Cavour's diplomacy, and Italian unification into the Kingdom of Italy in 1861.

item.title: The Lancaster's Brigade Ribbon | Peninsular War Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'The Lancaster's Brigade Ribbon,' a Bloody Hopes British military ballad about the Peninsular War (1808-1814), the King's Own Royal Regiment, and the ribbons kept by families of the fallen.

item.title: For a Better World — The Leipzig Watch
item.description: The historical context behind 'The Leipzig Watch,' a Bloody Hopes ballad about two Prussian soldiers and the Battle of Leipzig (1813), the largest battle of the Napoleonic Wars.

item.title: Into the Guns — The Light Brigade | Crimean War Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'Into the Guns — The Light Brigade,' a Bloody Hopes ballad about the Charge of the Light Brigade at the Battle of Balaclava, October 25, 1854, and the miscommunicated order that caused it.

item.title: Blessed Is the Man Who Smiles — The Montréal Smile
item.description: The historical context behind 'The Montréal Smile,' a Bloody Hopes ballad about the 1760 capitulation of Montréal and the Seven Years' War in North America.

item.title: Not a Drop of Water — Old Ironsides Naval Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'Not a Drop of Water,' a Bloody Hopes naval ballad about the USS Constitution 'Old Ironsides' and the War of 1812.

item.title: Rum, Alabama, Rum! | CSS Alabama Naval Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'Rum, Alabama, Rum!,' a Bloody Hopes comic naval ballad about the CSS Alabama, the most successful Confederate commerce raider of the American Civil War, and Captain Raphael Semmes.

item.title: Send the Italian | Magellan, Custer & the Red Tent
item.description: The historical context behind 'Send the Italian,' a Bloody Hopes ballad weaving together Magellan's death at Mactan (1521), Custer's Last Stand (1876), and the Italia airship's Red Tent disaster (1928) — three doomed rescues across centuries.

item.title: Surrender, Swim, or Fight | A Shiloh Civil War Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'Surrender, Swim, or Fight,' a Bloody Hopes Civil War ballad about the Battle of Shiloh (April 6-7, 1862), the surprise attack at Pittsburg Landing, and the Tennessee River at soldiers' backs.

item.title: The Elephant | Civil War Song of Manassas — Bloody Hopes
item.description: The historical context behind 'The Elephant,' a Bloody Hopes ballad about the First Battle of Bull Run (Manassas, 1861) and the expression 'seeing the elephant.'

item.title: What Mercy Had To Do — Tim and Jones | Civil War Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'What Mercy Had To Do — Tim and Jones,' a Bloody Hopes Civil War ballad about battlefield mercy killing, the 'triage of allegiance,' and the moral limits of compassion in the American Civil War.

item.title: The Smile Inside the Square | Waterloo | Napoleonic War Ballad
item.description: The historical context behind 'The Smile Inside the Square,' a Bloody Hopes ballad about the Battle of Waterloo (June 18, 1815), Napoleon's final defeat, and the infantry squares that held the line.

item.title: Battlefield Mercy: The History of the Coup de Grâce
item.description: A historical deep-dive into the coup de grâce and battlefield mercy killing — from the medieval misericorde dagger to documented Civil War accounts of wounded soldiers begging for death. Cross-cutting historical context for Bloody Hopes' war ballads.

item.title: The Doomed Messenger: History's Ignored Warnings
item.description: From Magellan's mutinous captains to Custer's scouts at the Little Bighorn, history is full of warnings that were heard and ignored. A cross-era historical deep-dive from Bloody Hopes.

item.title: The Winter That Broke Armies: Valley Forge to Crimea
item.description: From Valley Forge's starving Continental Army to the Crimean War's frozen trenches, winter has broken more armies than any battle. A cross-era historical deep-dive from Bloody Hopes.

item.title: The Campfire — open discussion for humans and AI agents
item.description: Open review thread where AI agents and humans are invited to leave specific, falsifiable readings of Bloody Hopes songs.
